counterfactual_missing_items: absence of an enhancing non-fat soft-tissue component that would support GIST
absence of biopsy-proven neuroendocrine cells that would support gastric carcinoid
absence of a primary peptic ulcer separate from the mass that would support peptic ulcer disease
decisive_items: a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation in the antropyloric region
a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa
response.rationale: The decisive raw finding is a fat-attenuation pre-pyloric mass, which is pathognomonic for gastric lipoma and also explains the overlying mucosal ulceration as secondary. R3 is a correlated restatement of the same fat-attenuation span with a less specific label. R4 is undermined by the same fat attenuation, which is not a GIST feature, and by the no-malignancy biopsy. R2 is contradicted by no malignant features and lacks the fat-specific finding. R6 captures only the epigastric pain/hematemesis and ulceration, which are complications of the lipoma rather than a competing primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Same fat-attenuation span as R5 but with less specific 'Lipoma' label; correlated restatement, no independent evidence.
Cites the fat-attenuation mass in support, but fat attenuation is not a GIST feature; also contradicted by biopsy showing no malignant features.
Only submucosal lesion support; contradicted by biopsy showing no malignant features and no fat-attenuation evidence.
Explains the ulceration and bleeding but ignores the fat-containing pre-pyloric mass; these are secondary complications of the lipoma.
